analytic.title: REDUCING OS OVERHEAD FOR REAL-TIME INDUSTRIAL CONTROLLERS WITH ADJUSTABLE TIMER RESOLUTION

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: In this paper, a new method, named Adjustable Timer Resolution (ATR) is proposed to control tasks timely, with enhanced performance on real-time operating systems. It prevents from useless execution of the timer Interrupt Service Routine (ISR). Features of the proposed method are compared with conventional method, and the schedulability is analyzed to estimate the performance. As an implementation model, uC/OS-11 is modified and ported to a PowerPC processor system. The metrics and results of the model are presented and discussed.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: There are numerous applications of the real-time system in the area of data monitoring, process control and communication. At the real-time system, time constraints must be satisfied because the data, which miss time constraints, are not only valueless but also sometimes harmful [l]. To meet the constraint, Operating System (OS) should support applications acquiring computation resources timely. Thus, the fine-grain task control and performance estimation are two of the most important features to design a real-time system.

A simple approach to get a fine control on conventional systems is reducing the time scale. Unfortunately, the approach results in making overhead because the time scale on the OS depends on the execution of the timer ISR.

In the time-sharing system, OS uses a periodic timer to distribute the CPU time to every task. The overhead from the timer ISR was not a serious problem on ordinary systems. The period of the timer is usually set from 1 ms to 20 ms, and the performance is accommodative enough. However, the timer ISR execution time makes problems on many real-time applications. Real-time applications usually require timers with microsecond precision. They need to be notified timely from OS about starting time and blocking time [2]. Moreover, although there are many systems based on the Personal Computer (PC), much more real-time systems based on the dedicated embedded system. The controllers of the systems are selected according to functions. As a result, relatively high performance controllers have been selected because the system may contain considerable overhead of OS.

To solve this problem, UTIME and Microtime were implemented [2,3]. Both of them add a new variabIe, usec, to get a thin time resolution within one time unit. However those provide thin control, the overhead of timer ISR execution time is still problems. Moreover, an extra timer is needed to keep track of the time. ATR method, proposed in this paper, provides fine control like UTIME and Micortime. However, ATR is different form those. It reduces timer intempt computation overhead and doesn't use an extra timer.

In this paper, ATR is proposed and discussed to deal with the problem, which comes from timer ISR execution. The method minimizes the overhead by changing from periodic invocation to on-demand invocation. To estimate the performance enhancement, the schedulability analysis is used with the comparison between fixed timer resolution method and ATR method. As the first example, ATR is implemented on uC/OS-11, the real-time kernel for microcontrollers and micro-processors. Experimental results show that ATR could provide fine control and improve the performance of the system without the help of additional hardware. ATR also do that by changing the kernel without modifying user tasks. It could be applied to increase the performance of real-time system with relatively low cost.

This paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, realtime OS is illustrated. The algorithm of ATR is presented in Section 3. In Section 4, the performance of ATR is analyzed. The implementation model and experimental results are presented in Section 5 and 6 . Finally, the conclusions are drawn in Section 7.

div.head: REAL-TIME OS
div.p: Real-time system is defined as the system which responses correctly and timely after extemal stimuli [ 1,2]. It usually consists of real-time OS and real-time application tasks. Real-time OS must provide independent tasks resources to meet their deadline. It usually runs tasks according to proper scheduling algorithms based on task priorities, which are assigned by the designer. Thus, to meet the dead line of more valuable functions, the OS gives up the execution from the lowest priority task, which is decided as relatively less significant. At any time, when it decide to run other tasks, it saves current information of tasklike registers, memory map, and various table and listsin the context area of the current task and restores that of the new task [4]. This context switching is occurred as two kinds of case. The first is blocking, this means the higher priority task releases the control of CPU to wait the determined time or events like semaphore, signal or message. The second is preemption, which means the running task is stopped by the higher priority task. Therefore preemption is not the voluntary work, The kemel should make the state of the running task ready and the highest ready task run by means of an interrupt. The periodic timer interrupt is a common way of implementing these preemptive schedulers. Figure 1 shows an example. When Task2 is running, Task2 is preempted by an ISR after time t , . This makes Taskl and Task3 ready. After the ISR, a scheduler of OS is called and checks which task is the highest ready task. So, Task2 becomes preempted and Taskl is run. After ts, Taskl blocks itself for an event or time delay and Task2, the highest ready task at this time, becomes run. At tI2 Taskl becomes ready by the timer ISR, Task2 is preempted again. Context switching is followed like that after t12. To implement these preemptive schedulers, priority comparison among ready tasks should be conducted after each ISR and blocking functions. Especially, in each timer ISR, the OS should -modify or compare waiting valuables of all waiting tasks to check the expiration of the waiting time. The periodic timer interrupt is an efficient way to check the arrival of higher priority tasks. Especially, sporadic tasks of which amval time is not regular could be guaranteed the anival time recognition bound by that as timer period [5]. However, many real-time applications need the ability to hack the time at the resolution of microseconds. Thus the conventional periodic method is not suitable.

div.head: ADJUSTABLE TIMER RESOLUTION
div.p: ATR designed based on following two things. First, realtime systems usually don't allow the creation and deletion of tasks during run-time. Moreover, the priority of the critical application task can have higher priority' than the kemel. When the highest priority task is running; there is no use to switch contexts because, if lower tasks become ready to run, lower tasks can't preempt the higher task. Thus, ATR method disables timer interrupt when the highest priority task is running. Figure 2 shows that. On the periodic timer method, the state of Tusk2 become ready and it is stored into the ready queue of OS after the timer ISR at t2. However, Task2 can't be run until the higher task, Taskl, is blocked (after t29). In spite of that, the periodic timer interrupt still intervene Taskl. On the contrary, ATR blocks the timer interrupt and get the better performance.

div.head: Algorithm
div.p: The detailed algorithm is shown in Figure 3. The system is assumed that it is the priority based real-time system on the uni-processor and preemptive multi-tasking environment. There is no task creation and deletion during run-time, and detailed task control is necessary. First, the system is started with the Time Resolution (TR), tuned as the longest period to minimize the number of timer interrupt services. If there is any time blocking function in the running task, the kemel computes the Expiring Time {ET) of the current task. And then, a time variable, which managed by kernel to carry tasks information about time, is updated as the summation of the time valuable and the difference of TR register value and Time Counter (TC) register value. Blocked higher tasks are searched and compared with the time valuable. If the higher priority task was blocked and expiring time is out of date, the state of task is changed to ready and TR is adjusted as the minimum value among expiring times of higher priority tasks. The expiring time of current task is updated as the summation of the time valuable and Delay Time (DT) of blocking function. After then, context switching function is called. If there is no higher priority task, TR and ET are adjusted as the summation of the time valuable and DT. And then, the context of the task is changed to the idle task. If the timer interrupt is occurred, that means the TR is expired. The time valuable is added as much as TR, and TR is adjusted as the expiring time of the highest priority task among ready tasks. Context switching is conducted to run the highest ready task.

div.head: Issues
div.p: ATR is a simple but rather new algorithm. There are several issues to be discussed before being adopted.

The first is the reliability problem. ATR prevents timer interrupt occurring during the assigned time. This may prevent blocking time checking of higher tasks. That is designed to change state of tasks from waiting to ready by modifying the timer valuable of each waiting task. But, if the algorithm is well implemented, unwanted blocking of higher tasks depends on only the probability of misexecuted instructions by unexpected reasons like EMI.

However, the problem is occurred on conventional OSs. The only difference is that the probability of ATR is accumulated. For example, unknown reasons, like noise, can make the blocking time of the highest task much larger than designed time by preventing timer interrupt. But that could be occurred at conventional OSs by mis-setting of the blocking time. In this case, the timer interrupt can occur, but context switching is not conducted because there is much time to run by mis-set the blocking variable. Though, unlike conventional OSs, the mis-execution of the second priority task could affect to the execution of the first priority task. Fortunately, the probability of those sorts of error is extremely small and those kinds of problems can be handled by the watch-dog timer.

The second problem is time skew. The time valuable of ATR irregularly updated as illustrated on Figure 4. OS usually keeps time as a global valuable, and updates at every timer ISR service. Thus the time value is kept with the skew range as much as the timer resolution. However, the time value is updated irregularly on ATR. To get the correct time, both of the timer register and the time valuable should be considered. Though this gives 1 or 2 more instruction computation time, time functions are not repeatedly used to get the computation results, and overhead of the functions small enough. The third is time drift. On the conventional OS, the time count register is reloaded by the timer itself, without any help from OS. Unlike periodic timer resolution method, on the ATR, the OS should reload the time count register. Thus, time leaking, from meeting the end of counting value to be re-loaded, takes place (Figure 4). It should be compensated when a new value is re-loaded into the timer resolution register.

The forth is the relation with event handling like semaphore, message queue and signal. On the real-time OS, event-handling functions always check waiting tasks to execute the higher ready task promptly. Because there is no direct relationship between the timer interrupt and the event handling mechanism, ATR doesn't affect the event handler except the event waiting time. The event waiting time is used to give the time limits of event waiting. But, these are implemented same as the blocking time. As a result, ATR doesn't affect the event handler and doesn't make additional overhead.

The fifth is the relationship with the round robin scheduling which assigns each task CPU time, fairly. The round robin method usually said that it isn't suitable to real-time system because it makes system hard to estimate. However, it is sometimes implemented because it is convenient to make a system. On an ATR system, round robin scheduling can be implemented on a certain priority level. In this case, if the assigned time slit of the same priority tasks is small, it is hard to get the performance enhancement from ATR.

div.head: Figure 4 Time Skew and Drift of ATR
div.p: The last is about the performance of ATR. A number of tasks usually require a lot of preemptions. Preemption in OS means an interrupt service, one of the most important performance elements of ATR. As a result, a great number of tasks reduce the benefit of ATR. Preemption threshold algorithm can be adopted to reduce it [ 6 ] . Detail analysis about performance will be discussed at the next section.

div.head: IMPLEMENTATION
div.p: uC/OS-I1 is firstly selected as the target OS. Although it has many restricted features like small numbers of tasks and non-supporting the priority inheritance protocol, it has simple architecture and relatively easy to modify [2].

In order to increase the resolution OSTime variable is changed as 64bit, OSETime. The 32bit valuable, OSTime is overflowed after 49 days when the timer resolution is Ims. Delay time computation mechanism is changed also. On the uC/OS, OSTCBDly keeps the remain, time of blocked tasks at every Task Control Block (TCB), which have information about each task. OSTCBDly is decremented at every timer ISR. In the ATR OSTCBDly is changed to OSTCBExpTime, and it keeps when the task should wake up. OSETimeDlyO is made similarly with OSTimeDlyO to manage these changed valuables. Pseudo code 1 shows that. It changes the state of the cufrent task ready, and updates TR according to the algorithm presented in Section 3.

div.head: EXPERIMENTS
div.p: In the first experiment, the precision of delay function is tested. One task is made to make delay 24.4ms. When the task is blocked, the default idle task of uC/OS-I1 is executed. After calling delay function the task compute some time to make uniform distribution from 0 to 24.4ms and delay 24.4ms. Figure 5 uC/OS-I1 which has the timer resolution of 22.4ms, shows uniform distribution form 0 to 24.72ms. The system of 12.2ms and 6.lms show similar results as uniform distribution between 12.52ms and 24.72ms, between 18.98 ms and 24.96ms, respectively. In case of 1.2ms and 0.6ms, they can provide relatively precise control but the times are shifted to 26.52ms and 29.12.
On the contrary, uC/OS with ATR shows better controls. The task woke up 996 times within from 24.44ms and 24.7ms, and woke up 4 times within from 24.7ms and 24.96ms(Figure 6)

Second example uses 6 tasks to compare the overhead of OSs. Each task accumulate global variable WorkLoad, 10 times and delay 97.6ms at the highest priority task, 48.8ms at the second priority task, 24.4ms at the third, 12.2ms at the forth and 6.lms at the fifth. The lowest priority task is doesn't delay itself and accumulate WorkLoad until it is preempted. Table 1 shows the computation time to make WorkLoad to Ox 100000.

div.head: CONCLUSION
div.p: In this paper, the ATR method is proposed and discussed about the issues. ATR prevents useless timer interrupt occumng to save CPU time with detailed task control. The performance is presented with a schedulability analysis. That shows the performance enhancement of ATR depends on the number of the preemption. To show the simplicity of the implementation, uC/OS-I1 is modified and ported on the evaluation board of which processor is MPC8260. Two experiments show that ATR could support more exact control and enhance performance.
The full implementation of ATR will be presented later. After testing event handling and time drift compensating functions, practical performance on practical applications will be presented.
